prompt_text: Who is the best personal injury lawyer in Atlanta for a car accident case?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t one universally “best” personal injury lawyer in Atlanta — the right attorney depends on your case details (injury severity, disputed liability, uninsured motorist issues, whether you need surgery, etc.), your preferences (trial lawyer vs. quick settlement), and how the lawyer communicates and handles cases. That said, here’s how to find the best lawyer for your car-accident case and what to look for.

What to prioritize
- Relevant experience: substantial experience handling car-accident cases (not just general civil practice).
- Trial experience: many cases settle, but you want someone willing and able to try the case if necessary.
- Proven results: settlements and verdicts for cases like yours (similar injuries, liability level).
- Resources: firm can pay medical liens, hire accident reconstructionists, experts, and cover litigation costs.
- Clear fee structure: contingency fee rates and how expenses are handled.
- Communication: timely responses and a clear point of contact.
- Local knowledge: familiarity with Georgia law, Atlanta judges, and local insurers.
- Client reviews and references: real client feedback, peer ratings (Martindale-Hubbell, Super Lawyers, Avvo).
- Clean disciplinary record: check Georgia Bar complaints/discipline.

Quick practical checks
- Georgia Bar search for license and disciplinary history.
- Martindale-Hubbell and Super Lawyers for peer/industry recognition.
- Google, Yelp, Avvo for client reviews.
- Ask for referrals from family/friends who had similar claims.

Typical fees and timing
- Contingency fees are common (often ~33%–40% depending on whether the case settles or goes to trial).
- Georgia personal-injury statute of limitations: generally 2 years from the date of injury (O.C.G.A. §9-3-33) — act promptly.

Questions to ask at a free consultation
- Have you handled cases like mine? What were the outcomes?
- Who will handle my case day-to-day?
- What is your contingency fee and how are expenses handled?
- Do you take cases to trial? How many times in the past few years?
- Can you provide recent client references or results?
- How will we communicate and how often?

Where to look for attorneys
- Georgia State Bar Lawyer Referral Service
- Super Lawyers (Georgia/Atlanta lists)
- Martindale-Hubbell peer review ratings
- Avvo and Google for reviews
- Better Business Bureau

If you want, I can:
- Provide a short list of top-rated Atlanta personal-injury firms (I’ll pull names based on directory reputations), or
- Help draft a message/email or phone script to use in consultations, or
- Suggest 3–5 attorneys near your ZIP code if you tell me your neighborhood and a few facts about the accident (injuries, disputed liability, insurance issues).

Which would you prefer?
